questions.question_text: A sales agent posts a property listing on social media without including the brokerage name. This is:
questions.correct_answer: A blind ad, which is prohibited
distractors: Permitted if the agent's name appears
questions.explanation: 61-2f-401(12)(b) and R162-2f-401h(1) require every advertisement to identify the brokerage name as shown on Division records. The only exception is an owner-agent advertising their own property that is not listed with their brokerage, identified as 'owner-agent' or 'owner-broker' (R162-2f-401h(3)).

questions.question_text: Under HB 419, when advertising a property online, the brokerage name must be:
questions.correct_answer: Within one click of the advertisement
distractors: Displayed on every page of the website
In the same font size as the listing
Included in the meta tags only
questions.explanation: H.B. 419 (effective May 7, 2025) amended 61-2f-401(12)(b): an online or digital advertisement satisfies the rule if it links to a website or media platform that identifies the brokerage name within one click. Non-digital ads must carry the brokerage name in the advertisement itself.

questions.question_text: An agent uses a team name in their advertising. Under Utah rules, what else must appear?
questions.explanation: R162-2f-401h(5) subjects a team, group, or other marketing entity to the same advertising requirements as an individual licensee, and R162-2f-401h(4) requires the brokerage name used to be the name shown on Division records.

questions.question_text: A sales agent posts on social media that they are a licensed real estate agent but does not advertise any specific property or service. Under HB 419, this post is:
distractors: A blind ad requiring brokerage name
Required to include the broker's name
questions.explanation: 61-2f-102(2)(b) excludes from 'advertisement' a social media post that generally identifies the person as being in the real estate profession, so long as it does not promote specific real estate, offer specific brokerage services, or specifically solicit the public to make contact. Any one of those three turns the post into an advertisement.

questions.question_text: All real estate advertising in Utah must be under the direction of the:
questions.explanation: R162-2f-401h(1) makes the licensee's advertising the principal broker's responsibility, and 61-2f-401(13) makes failure to exercise active and reasonable supervision over affiliated licensees an independent violation.

questions.question_text: A listing agent receives an offer but does not present it because they believe the price is too low. This is:
distractors: Required for offers under 80% of list price
Permitted if the seller is unavailable
questions.explanation: 61-2f-308(2)(a)(i) requires a principal broker under an exclusive brokerage agreement to accept delivery of and present to the client all offers and counteroffers. The licensee's own view of the price is irrelevant.

questions.question_text: A licensee learns a buyer already has a signed exclusive agreement with another brokerage but tries to sign the buyer anyway. This is:
distractors: Legal if the first agreement is over 30 days old
questions.explanation: R162-2f-401b(1)(k) bars a licensee from entering or attempting to enter a concurrent agency representation when the licensee knows or should know the principal already has an agency agreement with another licensee. R162-2f-401b(1)(j) separately bars exposing a principal to a double commission without informed consent.

questions.question_text: Since H.B. 419 (2025), who may sell factory built housing — a manufactured or mobile home — in Utah?
questions.correct_answer: A real estate licensee, or a dealer licensed under Title 58, Chapter 56
distractors: Only a real estate licensee, with no other option
Anyone; no license of any kind is required
Only a manufactured home dealer, never a real estate licensee
questions.explanation: H.B. 419 added factory built housing to the definition of principal broker activity in 61-2f-102(29)(a) and (b), except for a person licensed with the Division of Professional Licensing as a dealer under the Building Inspector and Factory Built Housing Licensing Act. So the sale needs either a real estate license or a DOPL dealer license.

questions.question_text: A buyer's agent tells a lender the buyer earns $120,000 when the buyer actually earns $80,000. This is:
distractors: Acceptable to help the buyer qualify
Only illegal if the loan closes
questions.explanation: 61-2f-401(1) bars substantial and intentional misrepresentation, and R162-2f-401b(1)(d) bars preparing or participating in a document the licensee knows does not reflect the true terms of the transaction. Inflating a buyer's income to a lender violates both, whether or not the loan closes.

questions.question_text: An agent purchases a property through their own listing without disclosing they are the buyer. This is:
distractors: Legal if a different agent writes the offer
questions.explanation: 61-2f-401(10) requires written disclosure of whether a purchase, sale, or rental is made for the licensee or for an undisclosed principal, and R162-2f-401a(5)-(6) require the licensee to reveal license status and any principal interest. R162-2f-401b(1)(o) also bars acting as a limited agent when the licensee is a principal.

questions.question_text: A licensee advises a client that they cannot show a property to a family with children because the neighborhood is not family-friendly. This violates:
questions.explanation: Steering on the basis of familial status violates the federal Fair Housing Act and the Utah Fair Housing Act (Title 57, Chapter 21), and a fair housing violation is dishonest dealing under 61-2f-401(16). Utah's protected classes go beyond the federal list.

questions.question_text: A licensee drafts a custom contract clause for a client instead of using an approved form addendum. This constitutes:
questions.explanation: 61-2f-306(1) limits licensees to filling out forms approved by the Commission and the Attorney General or prepared by legal counsel, R162-2f-401a(18) requires an approved addendum for any modification, and R162-2f-401b(1)(p) bars altering the REPC's printed or inserted language. Drafting original contract language is the unauthorized practice of law.

questions.question_text: Which obligation applies to all Utah licensees regardless of their role in a transaction?
distractors: Represent both buyer and seller equally
Provide legal advice on contract terms
questions.explanation: Every licensee must deal honestly. 61-2f-401(16) makes any conduct constituting dishonest dealing grounds for discipline, and 61-2f-401(1) covers misrepresentation. Licensees are not required to represent both sides, give legal advice, or inspect property.

questions.question_text: A licensee does not complete CE before the license expires but keeps showing property. This is:
distractors: Only a concern if a complaint is filed
Permitted if the CE is finished within 60 days
questions.explanation: CE is a condition of renewal (R162-2f-204(2)(b)). Once the license expires the individual may not act as a licensee — 61-2f-201 makes it unlawful, and 61-2f-302 requires an active affiliation. There is no grace period that allows practice on an expired license.

questions.question_text: A licensee accepts compensation from both the buyer and seller in a transaction without telling either party. This is:
distractors: Standard practice if both parties benefit
Legal if the amounts are equal
questions.explanation: 61-2f-401(2) makes acting for more than one party without the informed written consent of the parties a violation, and R162-2f-401a(16) requires written disclosure to each party of any compensation beyond the commission, with that compensation paid to the licensee's principal broker.
